| `MongoDBAtlasOrganizationCollection` | Collection of organizations in a resource group |

| `PlanName` | `string` | Required. Display name of the plan |
| `OrganizationName` | `string` | Name of the MongoDB Atlas organization |
| `ResourceNotFound` | Organization doesn't exist | Verify name and resource group |
| `AuthorizationFailed` | Insufficient permissions | Check RBAC roles on resource group |
| `InvalidParameter` | Missing required properties | Ensure all required fields are set |

content.user_title: Manage MongoDB Atlas Through Azure ARM
content.value_statement: Azure teams need clear guidance for managing MongoDB Atlas organizations through Azure ARM and Marketplace billing. This skill provides focused .NET SDK workflows, model references, and operational guardrails.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the Azure.ResourceManager.MongoDBAtlas package, GA version, API version, and ARM resource type.
Shows installation guidance for the MongoDB Atlas Azure SDK, Azure.Identity, and Azure.ResourceManager packages.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and ArmClient setup for Azure ARM access.
Outlines create, get, list, update, tag, and delete workflows for Atlas organization resources.
Documents key model properties, provisioning states, marketplace statuses, and common errors.
Highlights that clusters, databases, collections, and users require the MongoDB Atlas API.
limitations: It does not directly manage MongoDB Atlas clusters, databases, collections, or Atlas users.
It assumes valid Azure permissions, subscription details, resource groups, and Marketplace offer settings.
The examples are guidance and still require environment-specific testing before production use.
It reflects the SDK and API versions documented in the skill file.

use_cases.title: Provision Atlas Organizations
use_cases.description: Plan Azure ARM creation of MongoDB Atlas organizations with Marketplace billing details and admin user information.

use_cases.title: Review Marketplace Configuration
use_cases.description: Validate publisher, offer, plan, term, and subscription details before creating an organization resource.

use_cases.title: Build .NET Management Flows
use_cases.description: Use SDK workflow guidance for authentication, resource lookup, tagging, updates, deletion, and long-running operations.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation before using the SDK.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what this skill can and cannot manage for MongoDB Atlas through Azure ARM. Include prerequisites and where cluster management starts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Setup Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing a .NET project for Azure ARM integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a short setup plan for using Azure.ResourceManager.MongoDBAtlas in a .NET service. Include packages, authentication, and required Azure details.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Organization Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning implementation for organization lifecycle operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a workflow to create, list, update, and monitor a MongoDB Atlas organization with Azure.ResourceManager.MongoDBAtlas. Call out long-running operations.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before applying an Azure ARM change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned Azure ARM MongoDB Atlas organization change for operational risk. Check subscription details, offer settings, RBAC, tags, and deletion risk: [paste plan]

output_examples.input: Summarize the package and resource scope.
output_examples.output: A concise summary of package name, GA version, API version, ARM resource type, and unsupported Atlas resource areas.

output_examples.input: Plan creation of a new Atlas organization through Azure ARM.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering credentials, resource group access, marketplace details, admin user details, organization name, tags, and completion handling.

output_examples.input: Help troubleshoot an organization deployment failure.
output_examples.output: A focused review of provisioning state, Azure RBAC, required properties, Marketplace subscription status, and offer configuration.

best_practices: Confirm subscription, resource group, location, and Marketplace offer details before creating resources.
Use async SDK methods and handle long-running operations with explicit completion or polling logic.
Review RBAC, tags, billing impact, and deletion scope before production changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for Atlas clusters, databases, collections, or Atlas user management.
Do not copy placeholder subscription IDs, emails, plan IDs, or organization names into production.
Do not run update or delete operations without confirming the target resource and business owner.

faq.question: Can this skill manage MongoDB Atlas clusters?
faq.answer: No. It covers Atlas organizations as Azure ARM resources. Use the MongoDB Atlas API for clusters and database resources.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented examples use DefaultAzureCredential and require suitable Azure RBAC permissions.

faq.question: What SDK version does it describe?
faq.answer: The skill documents Azure.ResourceManager.MongoDBAtlas version 1.0.0 with API version 2025-06-01.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this replace production testing?
faq.answer: No. Treat the examples as implementation guidance and validate them against your Azure tenant and Marketplace setup.

faq.question: What are the main operational risks?
faq.answer: Incorrect Marketplace offer details, missing Azure permissions, wrong target resource groups, and unreviewed delete operations are the main risks.
